title: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares detained by ICE officials in Texas
content:
Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares is being detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officials in Texas.

In a post on X on Sunday, the 41-year-old Venezuelan wrote: “ICE has me at the Texas border crossing. This is crazy.”

ICE’s online Detainee Locator System shows that Linares is in ICE custody at the El Paso Processing Center.

In a statement shared on X by journalist Ricardo Celis, Linares’ legal team, immigration specialists Wilner & O’Reilly, wrote that Linares is “in the United States legally and has cooperated fully with the authorities.

“We are working closely with ICE and the Department of Homeland Security to resolve this matter as quickly as possible.

“Immigration proceedings follow established procedures, which naturally take time. We are confident in Mr. Linares’s position and expect this matter to be resolved once the process concludes.

“Out of respect for his privacy and the legal process, we will not be providing further comments regarding the details of his case at this time.”

On Monday, WBA president Gilberto Mendoza posted on X, confirming Linares is in ICE custody and offering his support.

He said: “Immigration attorneys are handling his case, and I am in constant contact with his family. As WBA President, I will always support our champions, in and out of the ring. Stay strong, Jorge.”

Linares retired from professional boxing in 2023 after losing to Britain’s Jack Catterall, with a record of 47 wins and 9 defeats in a career spanning 21 years.

He fought 13 times as a professional in the U.S., including bouts against Devin Haney in Las Vegas and Vasiliy Lomachenko in New York and claimed world titles at featherweight, super-featherweight and lightweight.
